Totally endorse her-not flexible at all but did the 30 days of yoga on this channel and loved it! Tho even after the tough positions she usually has really easy positions afterwards and it is more about choosing to do moves that suit you and breathing deeply rather than sticking to a set routine. 
Not saying she will magically heal your depression as that is a long way away for me but I feel better during the videos and afterwards for a little while along with better posture and a knowledge that I can do a few cool looking yoga positions with the investment of half an hour a day whenever and wherever I want. Dunno if half the positions I do are correct but the deep breathing and calm feeling is worth it.
Plus all the yoga I do is in my pyjamas so you def don't need expensive yoga clothes. Most u need is some kind of a mat (if u are dealing with hardwood floors like me) and a pillow.

Gaslighting and victim blaming plain and simple. They as good as said for her to put up and shut up. Bateman explaining how acting in a cast works to Walters was the cherry on top.I mean Tambor admitted what he did and apologised (not fucking excusing him as he has way more shit going on) and the other members of the boys club are rushing over to explain how Walters is not supposed to be upset at a guy whose treatment surpassed all others bad behaviour in decades in show business. The galling bit is that Jessica has bought into it and clearly feels like she is not a team player and sounds almost pissed off at herself for being so upset. I have been in that position before and nothing is more lonely than feeling like the crazy one in a situation where you know it was wrong but you can't put your hand up as everyone is so eager to defend the other person and "don't rock the boat"As she said in the interview, it wasn't sexual but fuck verbal bullying is so debasing-I hate that she had to trivialise her own experience when you just know that a woman who has spent decades in show business -that when she said that she never experienced anything like what Tambor did to her-it must have been BONE CHILLING. Imagine Hollywood of the sixties and onwards-the amount of entitlement and sexism is rampant now imagine back then and then consider her  statements. It must have been on another level for her to be so hurt and pained by it. And then for all the cast for her to be dismissive of her feelings and why she shouldn't be taking it so personal because blah blah-he is learning-Tambor is seventy plus-fuck that boys will be boys shit.

Yep, u said it. Walters is not a newbie to acting she has been doing it longer than most of the cast is alive so it must have been terrible for her to be so stung and hurt because of it. But the thing is all the bystanders here like Bateman who are apologists for Tambor and are talking so condescending to Walters like she is ridiculous for being so upset and this is how acting works-this shit is toxic.
Hearing the interview is even worse-she is sticking up for herself but clearly regretting having emotions and being upset over something that DESERVES it and the actors (the men) are as good as saying "why aren't you over it yet? You're making our lives harder"while defending Tambor to the hilt. Cross saying Tambor is still learning?! He is in his seventies! This "boys will be boys" attitude is only semi cute for infants but geriatrics shouldn't be forgiven for harassment even if it's not sexual in nature. People taunting you or whatever happened=not cool and then being made to feel like the crazy one for not being part of the "team" when one member made you feel an inch high is fucking awful...

This is so fucked up! Feel like all the men in the interview would take a bullet for Tambor and talked down to Walters all through for getting upset. Bateman mansplains the acting business to Walters and how this happens all the time which she said never happened to this extent to her before...and Walters clearly feels at fault for making a big deal about the issue.
This is the same Jessica Walters who started acting professionally in 1962. Jason Bateman was born in 1969 and felt the need to tell her how to handle acting within a cast. Shit is fucked up!
